note: Goods on the world market (gameplay values). Civilian factories make consumer goods (the consumer-goods share set by the economic system law) and industrial goods (factories not busy with construction); refineries make fuel. Demand follows GDP and industry and is scaled through 2000 so world supply and demand balance at a price of 1. Prices move toward (demand / supply) ^ elasticity. Surpluses are sold along trade routes; deficits are bought. Trade income changed since 1 January 2000 moves growth, so the World Bank 2000 calibration is kept.

goods.name: Consumer goods
goods.description: Clothing, electronics, cars and household goods.

goods.name: Industrial goods
goods.description: Machinery, steel, chemicals and components for industry and construction.

goods.name: Fuel
